questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Arrogance.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• **'Arrogance' **is a word derived from the Latin word** 'arrogans' **meaning insolent, overbearing, presumptuous.
 
• Let us look at the** correct spelling** and **meaning** of the given word:-
 
 
• **Arrogance***(noun)* - offensive display of superiority or self-importance; overbearing pride.
 
• For Example - When the guardsman rose, the **arrogance** was gone from his face, replaced by anger.
 
 

**Therefore, the correct spelling of the given word is ***'Arrogance'*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Antonyms **of arrogance - humble, lowly, modest, meek.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement”.**

I wondered what one would have thought some 40 years ago if you (had said) you could heat liquid using a plastic container.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** No Improvement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• The sentence is talking about something that the person had said 40 years ago i.e.** a long time ago.**
 
• Past Perfect Tense is used to express an action that has been completed(a long time ago) in the past.
 
 
• Structure - **Subject + had + V₃ + Object**.
 
• For Example - He** had left** for U.S.A.
 
 
 
• Therefore, 'had said' is correct and the sentence requires no further improvement.

**Thus, the correct sentence is ***I wondered what one would have thought some 40 years ago if you** had said **you could heat liquid using a plastic container.*

questions.question: Was achieved. ______ you wanted the flame.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** If**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• In the above given blank, **'if' **will be used.
 
• It is so because it is a **conditional sentence**.
 
• Conditional sentences are statements discussing known factors or hypothetical situations and their consequences. Complete conditional sentences contain a conditional clause (often referred to as the if-clause) and the consequence.
 
• **Consider the following sentences:-**
 
 
• **If** a certain condition is true, then a particular result happens.
 
• I would travel around the world** if** I won the lottery.
 
 
 
• **'Nor'** cannot be used because it is mostly used with neither and when used alone it should be preceded by a negative sentence which is not the case in the above given paragraph.
 
• **'So'** and **'thus'** are not apt for the given blank.

**Therefore, the correct answer for the given blank is*** If*.

questions.question: Would spread ______ a loud noise
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** With**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:- 

__
 
• **'With' **is a preposition which is used for different purposes.
 
• With meaning** 'having'** - We use with to mean** ‘having’** or** ‘possessing’.**
 
• **For Examples:-**
 
 
• It’s the house **with **the really big gates.
 
• She woke **with** terrible toothache.
 
 
 
• Here in the sentence the burner flame would spread having a loud noise.
 
• **Within** - It is used to denote time or position which is inside the range or limits of a particular period of time or distance.
 
• For Example - My house is** within **a mile of the station.
 
• **At** - It is used to denote a particular position or a particular place(or time)
 
• For Example - I am** at** my house.
 
• **During** - It is used to denote a period of time in which something happens.
 
• For Example - I was in Delhi **during** the winter.

**Therefore, the correct answer for the blank is* ****With*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Different uses of With:-

With meaning ‘in the same place as’

With means ‘in the same place as someone or something’ or ‘accompanying’:

She arrived with her boyfriend.|

I don’t like tea with milk.

There was a free phone with the car.

With: reactions and feelings

With often follows adjectives which refer to reactions and feelings:

Are you happy with your music lessons?

The teacher got angry with them because they were behaving badly.

I’m delighted with this new jacket.

With meaning ‘using’

We use with to refer to what we use to do something:

They opened the package with a knife.

I’ll tie it with some tape to keep it closed.

He cleaned the table with a cloth he found in the kitchen.

With meaning ‘having’

We use with to mean ‘having’ or ‘possessing’:

It’s the house with the really big gates.

She woke with terrible toothache.

The Commonwealth Institute used to be a building with a very unusual roof in Kensington.

With meaning ‘because of’

Spoken English:

We use with to mean ‘because of’ or ‘as a result of’. This is especially common in speaking:

With all this work, I’d better stay in tonight.

I couldn’t sleep with the noise of the traffic.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

Sneha said to Arjun, “Go away.”

options.text: Sneha ordered Arjun to go away.
Sneha asked Arjun that he should go away
Sneha say to Arjun to go away
Sneha inquired Arjun to go away

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Sneha ordered Arjun to go away**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• The reported speech has a sense of order and not question or inquiry.
 
• It is so because Sneha is ordering Arjun that he should leave.
 
• Therefore, **asked** and** inquired **cannot be used in the case of ordering.
 
• **'Say to'** cannot be used because the reported verb should be in past tense and not in present tense.
 
• Therefore, by elimination method we can eliminate option 2,3 and 4.

**Thus, the correct indirect speech of the given sentence is ***Sneha ordered Arjun to go away*.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

The _____ of many archaic and dilatory procedures have proved to be extremely damaging to our governance and society.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Imposition**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• In the above given sentence, **'imposition'** will be used. 
 
• The context is saying that the practice and imposing of old fashioned ways and slow actions have affected the governance and society.
 
• Thus, imposition is the apt word for the blank.
 
• **Imposition***(noun) *- a situation in which someone expects another person to do something that they do not want to do or that is not convenient.
 
• For Examples:- 
 
 
• I hope the drive to the airport isn’t an **imposition**.
 
• Would it be too much of an** imposition** to ask you to pick my parents up from the airport?
 
 
 
• **Caution***(noun)* - great care, because of possible danger
 
 
• For Example -Any advertisement that asks you to send money should be treated with** caution**.
 
 
 
• **Translation***(noun) *- to change something especially language.
 
 
• For Example - He specializes in** translation** from Danish into English.
 
 
 
• **Revolution***(noun)* - A great change or also means to rotate.
 
 
• For Example - The American** Revolution** was a great turning point in the history of America.
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer for the blank is** *Imposition*.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• In the above given sentence, **'one of the worst' **will be used.
 
• The context talks about categorizing cars as worst.
 
• It is so because the sentence is talking about a comparison of multiple cars with a car which cannot be expressed by** 'the worst'**.
 
• If 'the worst' had to be used, then 'cars' would be replaced by 'car'.
 
• **'Worst'** needs to be preceded by** 'the' **and still it will qualify a car and not multiple cars.
 
• Thus, 'worst' is also wrong.
 
• 'Mostly worst' is **erroneous** and **invalid** grammatically.

**Therefore, the correct answer for the blank is ***One of the worst.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

She has (1)/reduced her (2)/consumption to considerably. (3)/No error (4)
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **3**.**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• A preposition is always followed by **a noun or a pronoun.**
 
• That noun is called the **object** of the preposition.
 
• Here,** 'to'** cannot be used because considerably is an adverb meaning by a notably large amount or to a notably large extent; greatly.
 
 
• For Example - Things have improved **considerably **over the last few years.
 
 
 
• Note that a verb** can't be the object of a preposition.

**Therefore, the correct sentence is*** She has reduced her consumption considerably.*
